Case Study: A Skateboard Ramp Profile

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

A local skate park is casting a concrete quarter-pipe. Seen from the side, the curved face of the ramp follows the parabola y=(x²)/4, where x is the horizontal distance in metres measured from the foot of the ramp and y is the height. The face begins at the origin and runs to x=4 m, where a vertical back wall closes the ramp. The site engineer needs the area of this shaded side cross-section, because the volume of concrete is that area multiplied by the 3 m width of the ramp. She also wants to compare the concrete used in the far half of the ramp with the near half, and to know what fraction of a plain 4 m×4 m square panel the curved region actually fills. Every figure she needs comes from a single definite integral of y with respect to x.
